name: One station
why: [0]: no other station, so the total is 0.

name: A line of four
why: [6, 4, 4, 6]: from station 0 the distances are 1, 2 and 3; from station 1 they are 1, 1 and 2.

name: Lengths matter
why: [14, 12, 22]. Each road counts with its length: moving from 1 to 2 adds the road's length 10 for the 2 stations left behind and takes it off for the 1 below. A solution that counts roads instead of lengths gives [3, 2, 3].

name: A star
why: [4, 7, 7, 7, 7]: the centre is 1 from each; a leaf is 1 from the centre and 2 from the other three leaves.

name: Roads listed the other way round
why: [23, 14, 17, 18, 24]. Roads are not listed parent first, and station 0 is a leaf here. Build the tree by a search from one station; do not assume the first number of a road is the parent.

name: A road of length 0
why: [7, 7, 14]: stations 0 and 1 are at the same place, 7 from station 2. A road of length 0 still joins two stations.

name: The figure's tree, with lengths
why: [11, 13, 15, 15, 19, 19, 21, 21], as in the figure of lesson 1 (A to H are 0 to 7).

name: A long line
expr: (lambda r: [len(r), sum(r), max(r), min(r), r[0], r[-1]])(total_distance(*args))
show: 100,000 stations in a row; road k joins k and k + 1 and is k % 7 + 1 long
why: The answer is checked as [n, sum, largest, smallest, first, last]. Station 0 is 99,999 roads from the far end: a recursive search stops at about 1,000 levels, and a search from every station is about 10¹⁰ steps. Use a BFS order and two passes.

name: 100,000 stations, random
expr: (lambda r: [len(r), sum(r), max(r), min(r), r[0], r[-1]])(total_distance(*args))
show: 100,000 stations; road v joins v to a random earlier station, with a length from 1 to 1,000, written either way round
why: A search from every station costs n² = 10¹⁰ steps. Rerooting is O(n).

name: A broom
expr: (lambda r: [len(r), sum(r), max(r), min(r), r[0], r[-1]])(total_distance(*args))
show: a line of 50,000 stations with 50,000 more all joined to its far end
why: Deep (50,000 levels) and wide at once. Recursion fails here; so does anything quadratic.
